problem_type: Main-process event loop parked on a synchronous child-process wait
symptom: 0.23.1: while results land, the app stops responding — clicks do nothing and Settings does not open right away; the user reports other versions do not feel this way.
direct_cause: electron/assets/generatedMediaDecode.ts ran ffmpeg with spawnSync in the main process to verify every generated output before it was written (wait ceiling 12–120 s by size). Every sync IPC from the renderer, every async IPC reply and window event waited behind it. History: a synchronous decode check already existed in v0.22.5 (inside projectAssetStore); v0.23.0 (#938, 8ddb06250) moved it to generatedMediaDecode.ts, switched it to a framehash decode and raised the size-scaled wait ceiling to 120 s, making the wait heavier; v0.23.1 inherits it.
class_root: Nothing structurally stops main-process code from waiting synchronously on an external process (spawnSync is as easy to write as spawn and passes every small-fixture test). The first remediation then made the opposite mistake: to move one wait off the main loop it turned the shared synchronous write boundary (19 doors) asynchronous, which silently changed the timing, atomicity and cleanup contract every caller relied on; independent verification found five regressions over three rounds. The invariant is: only the wait is asynchronous; publishing stays a synchronous atomic step whose input can only be a verified staged artifact.
affected_population: Every generated image / video / audio written through writeAsset, writeDeterministicAsset, moveAssetFile or copyAssetFile with meta.kind=generated (provider results, MCP materialization, Codex / Antigravity / Dreamina local results, custom calls, screenshots, frame extraction, trim, depth video, camera-move)
All platforms; worst on large videos, slow disks and machines with real-time antivirus scanning
entry_points: generatedAssetStaging.prepareVerifiedGeneratedAsset: the only producer of VerifiedStagedAsset (async: pin, capture identity, stage, verify)
projectAssetStore.publishVerifiedGeneratedAsset: the only consumer (sync: re-assert identity, renameSync, sidecar, broadcast)
writeGeneratedAsset / writeGeneratedDeterministicAsset / storeAssetBytes / copyAssetFile(generated): the entries that run both steps
writeAsset / moveAssetFile: synchronous boundary, restored to main, refuses kind:generated
LocalTaskJobs.query: single-flight import for the Antigravity local provider

external_sources.purpose: Electron performance guide: the main process must not block on I/O or long work; use asynchronous child processes.

execFile timeout / maxBuffer / killed semantics used to map the asynchronous run back onto the existing verdict facts (also verified empirically with a real child for timeout, maxBuffer, non-zero exit and ENOENT).

invariants: Main-process production code under electron/ never waits synchronously on an external process (spawnSync / execFileSync / execSync count is zero outside one path-listed E2E fixture).

Only the decode wait is asynchronous: the synchronous write boundary keeps the main-branch contract for every non-generated caller (returns after the file is in place; move by rename; uploads by staging + link).

A generated output is published only as a VerifiedStagedAsset: its bytes were pinned before any await, staged privately under the project root, verified on that staged file, and published by a synchronous same-volume renameSync. The verified file is the published file, and a failure never leaves a partial file at the published path.
The project identity is captured before the wait and re-asserted synchronously right before the rename; a rebound project refuses the write.
The publish step is one synchronous critical section (no await between identity check, path choice, rename and sidecar), so concurrent publishes of one deterministic asset cannot interleave.
A local task's import is single-flight: overlapping queries share one import and cancellation waits for it to settle.

Every in-flight generated staging has an owner for its whole life: a controlled quit aborts it (killing the decoder child) and removes its staging directory before exit; staging left by a process that is gone (crash, kill, quit budget exhausted) is reclaimed when the project is next opened, judged by the owning process id rather than only by age.

door_reduction.why_not: Each door is a distinct product entry (provider retrieval, renderer import, MCP materialization, local providers, screenshots, frame / trim / depth / camera-move tools). They are not merged because they already converge on one pair of boundaries: prepareVerifiedGeneratedAsset (only producer of VerifiedStagedAsset) and publishVerifiedGeneratedAsset (only consumer); the synchronous writers refuse kind:generated, so no door can publish a generated output any other way. Staging creation (createUploadStagingDir / createUploadStagingDirSync) and the project-open sweep are new doors by design: every .nomi-upload-* directory now has an owning process and a live registration.

generality_proof: The decode verdict has one caller (generatedAssetStaging.verifyStagedGeneratedContent). Every generated output reaches disk only through publishVerifiedGeneratedAsset, whose only accepted input type is produced only by prepareVerifiedGeneratedAsset; writeAsset and moveAssetFile throw on kind:generated, so a new caller cannot skip verification or the staged publish. Non-generated callers see exactly the main-branch synchronous contract, which removes the class of caller-timing regressions (V-1208-3) instead of patching callers one by one. The broader class (any synchronous child wait in the main process) is closed by the check-heavy-path rule.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The only way the decode check runs ffmpeg: an asynchronous child with timeout kill and output cap.
Async half: pin bytes, capture AssetWriteContext, stage privately under the project root, verify the staged file; only producer of VerifiedStagedAsset.
Sync half: re-assert identity, renameSync same-volume atomic publish, sidecar, broadcast; always removes the staging directory.
Single-flight import so an asynchronous import cannot interleave with a second query or a cancellation.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: prepare + publish with materialization key; concurrent same-key tests in projectAssetStore.test.ts.
Generated branch stages from the source path, verifies the staged copy, renames; source-overwrite test.
Main-branch contract restored (rename); refuses kind:generated; browser import closed loop in browserImportCommit.test.ts.
E2E fixture renderer; only constructed when isProductionRunE2eFixtureEnabled. Listed by exact path in the gate exemption.

recurrence.reason: Any future local media step (transcode, probe, extract) can reach for a synchronous child-process call; it passes every test on small fixtures and only freezes on user machines.
same_class_scan: rg -n '\b(spawnSync|execFileSync|execSync)\b' electron --type ts: 2 production files (generatedMediaDecode.ts — fixed; productionRunE2eFixture.ts — gated fixture, exempted by path)
electron/offLedgerEgress.structure.test.ts AST scan of child-process-sync primitives: same two files
node scripts/door-map.mjs verifyGeneratedMediaDecodes / validatedGeneratedMeta / writeAsset / writeDeterministicAsset / moveAssetFile

prevention.invariant: Generated outputs reach disk only as VerifiedStagedAsset through publishVerifiedGeneratedAsset (type-level: only prepareVerifiedGeneratedAsset produces it; runtime: synchronous writers refuse kind:generated). electron/ production code contains no synchronous child-process wait outside the path-listed E2E fixture (check:heavy-path main-sync-child-process, baseline 0).
prevention.failure_mode: check:heavy-path exits 1 and prints file:line with the asynchronous replacement.
prevention.strategy: Keep the shared write boundary synchronous and atomic for everyone; isolate the only asynchronous step (staging + verification) behind a branded artifact that the synchronous publish requires. The decode check only exists in asynchronous form and the gate forbids synchronous child waits.

legacy_paths.rationale: The spawnSync decoder and the synchronous writeDeterministicAsset are deleted (the first-round asynchronous write boundary never reached main and is gone from this branch); generated outputs have exactly one publish path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Node's built-in child_process.execFile replaces spawnSync; no third-party runtime is involved and the bundled ffmpeg and its invocation are unchanged.

migration: No stored data changes. Generated-output callers switched to writeGeneratedAsset / writeGeneratedDeterministicAsset (already async contexts); non-generated callers are back on the main-branch synchronous calls. Abandoned staging directories from an interrupted prepare are reclaimed by reapAbandonedUploadStaging.
residual_risks: Pre-existing synchronous writes on the main branch remain for non-generated byte imports (writeAsset writes the caller buffer with writeFileSync) and the deterministic existing-file hash (readFileSync); out of scope here, tracked as performance guide M02.
prepareVerifiedGeneratedAsset copies a caller buffer once before staging (one transient extra copy for large byte inputs).
An asynchronous decode spawned inside a paid dispatch is visible to the dispatch ledger child_process channel, which can only make a failed dispatch read as unknown (conservative).

A staging copy that is still being written when the quit budget runs out (the copy step is not abortable mid-stream) is left on disk; it is reclaimed on the next project open because its owning process is gone.
